utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Good morning, your Honour. Your Honours, yesterday you asked a question about the witness Klipic and whether she had known or asked who had killed the eleven policemen at that spot. We had checked her testimony and she had made no mention of that in the course of her testimony. I do not know whether your Honour still wants to pursue it; if you do, she is available and can be recalled.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: No, I do not think so. I do not know. Let me confer. No, I think we have decided not to take that road. Thank you though. Would you bring in the witness, please? FIKRET KADIRIC, recalled.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, while we are waiting for the witness, there is another matter. The next witness to be called in order would be the witness that we are seeking confidentiality for, so if we could then go into closed session I will make the application and we will proceed from there, if that is convenient to the Court?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. We will do that. Mr. Kadiric, you understand that you are still under the oath that you took yesterday to tell the truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. Thank you. Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Kadiric, Zoran Cvijic who had already been employed in the administration department of the Prijedor traffic police when you became Commander of the traffic police, can you tell us for how long he had held that position before you became Commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was not employed there. He was temporarily appointed to that particular duty, up until the moment when his final duty would be decided on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell us then how long he had been temporarily appointed to the administration department before you became Commander of the traffic police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly, but it could have been for some two or three months.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you became Commander of the traffic police, you did not remove him from that position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: He remained in that position until your work at the Prijedor police station was no longer possible?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: During the time that you worked with him, you had no cause to doubt his honesty?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, because there was another employee who was helping, the one who was in charge of all the administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you worked with him he carried out your commands?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was rarely giving him direct orders because there was an employee, administrative employee, who was helping him in case he had too many things to do. Personally, I do not think he had too many things to do and there was no real reason for him to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That is all I ask.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No questions, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to Mr. Kadiric being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kadiric, you are permanently excused. You are free to leave. Thank you for coming.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. Can we go into closed session?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you for helping us. I forgot just that quickly. We will need to stand in recess for five minutes to go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I should have indicated earlier (and I apologise for not doing so) that the witness Nasiha Jakupovic will not be called to give evidence. Her testimony is going to be covered by other witnesses. I had thought that the list we filed with the Court did not have the name on it, but I understand that it was on there and she will not be called as a witness.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. Thank you. Mr. Tieger, would you call your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. The next witness is Sofia Tadic. SOFIA TADIC, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Would you please take the oath that is being handed to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You may be seated. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, you may begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Ma'am, what is your name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sofia Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 1st November 1957.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Osijek.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is that in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Croatia, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How long did you live in Osijek?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 14 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After that did you move with your family to Munich, Germany?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in '72.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Three years later in 1975 did you meet Mladen Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you and Mladen Tadic married in 1978?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were you married?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where did you and Mladen live after your marriage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Munich.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you and Mladen visit Kozarac while you were living in Munich?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How often would you visit Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Often, often for all holidays, often just for weekends.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: For approximately what period of time during the course of a year might you be in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sometimes, as I said, just for weekends, holidays, three or four weeks during the summer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Would you be in Kozarac as much as two months in the course of some years?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On average, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How long did you continue to do that? When was your last visit to Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In March of 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you eventually divorced from Mladen Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When was that, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We divorced in Prijedor in December of '91 and in Munich in '92.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you visited Kozarac where would you stay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the house of Mladen's parents.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you come to know the members of Mladen's family and their family members?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were there some members of the family whom you came to know better?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Which members of the family were those?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Family members who lived in that house.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did that include Mladen's brother Dule and Dule's wife Mira?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: During the time that you knew them, did they always live in the home of the parents of Mladen and Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not the whole time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where else did they live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They lived for a few months, as far as I recall, for a few months they were subletting a place a couple of streets down.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did they also spend any time outside of the country abroad during the time that you were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, in Libya.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Ma'am, when you first met and got to know the Tadic family in the late 1970s, did they have any apparent interest in or involvement in Serbian nationalist issues?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was there some indirect expression of that interest by family members?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Indirect, yes, but not from there, from them personally, but from the family that lived farther down.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At some point did members of the Tadic family and, in particular, Dule Tadic, begin to express some interest in or involvement in Serbian nationalist issues?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: About when did that begin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It began, as far as I could tell, at a time when Mira was pregnant. They said if it would be a boy it would be called "Slobodan" after Slobodan Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was she pregnant with their first child or their second child at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The second.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did they express any other feelings about Slobodan Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With expressions like Milosevic was the only real man, the only real politician, in the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did they talk about events in former Yugoslavia at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did they say about certain events that were happening at that period?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The conversations revolved around events that were going on in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was said about Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Comments like that Serbs should be brought to Kosovo so that the Albanians would be repressed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were these comments by Dule Tadic and other members of the family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was this new interest in things Serbian expressed in any other ways that you noticed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Towards the end of my coming, my visits to Kozarac, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: First of all, may I ask you, had the family been religiously oriented or involved in religion when you first met them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, they were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Around the time that you mentioned in the late 80s, did the family become involved in the Serbian Orthodox church?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was there an interest in, for example, particular expressions of religion in baptisms or festivals, things like that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they went to church for holidays and there was conversation about having the children baptised finally.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Kozarac was a predominantly Muslim community, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: From what you observed, did Dule Tadic have many Muslim friends?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What about Emir Karabasic, did you know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How close were Emir Karabasic and Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not close at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did they associate together?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they visited.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: From what you observed, did you see the kinds of intimate exchanges and warmth that you normally associate with a close friendship?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you become aware of Dule Tadic's attitude toward the Muslims of Kozarac generally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And what sorts of things did he say or do that indicated to you his view toward Muslims generally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As an example, when we were standing in the yard and people were going to the mosque, there were comments like, "The Balijas are going to the mosque".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The term "balija" is an offensive term for Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, offensive.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: A term which is not used in polite company?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not normally, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you become aware or familiar with Dule Tadic's temperament? Was he an even tempered man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did find out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What were you able to observe about his temperament or temper?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Rather violent, then peaceful.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: For example, did you have to watch yourself in any way around the house not to trigger any kind of expressions of temper on his part?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Personally, no, because I was there with my husband, but the others, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you observe any incidents when, in fact, his temper was triggered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you describe any of those, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On one occasion we heard yelling and arguing from the next room where Mira and Dule -- Mira and Dule lived, and Mira, I saw her the next day and she had black and blue on her face, marks.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you recall any other occasions where you became aware of Dule Tadic's acts of temper and violence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Another occasion also when we were giving a ride to Dule and another man in our car, it came to blows in the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: First of all, where was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Munich.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who was in the car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My daughter, my then husband Mladen, Dule and that man.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did an argument begin between Dule and someone else in the car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: An argument started before we got into the car and it ended up in the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was the argument about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The argument started at a sports event and I do not know how it started, but the argument broke out in front of the car and then ended in the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As the argument continued in the car, what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The argument turned into a fight.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Exactly what occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I turned around, I saw Dule hitting that man with his hand in the face, and the second time I turned I saw him grabbing him by the genitals and squeezing him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were all of you going in the car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were giving a ride to Dule and this man to where they were staying the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Why was Dule in Munich at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was working.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you arrived at the place where Dule Tadic and this man were staying the night, what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We all got out and then Dule jumped over a fence, went to this house where they were staying. It was a prefabricated building, and he took a canister with gasoline and started splashing it around the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: He was still angry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After he started doing that, did someone intervene and stop him from continuing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mladen got involved and he tried to calm him down, whereupon Dule went out. There was some wood that was piled in front of it and then he started hitting it with his hands, that pile of wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Why was he doing that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Most probably out of anger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After your last visit to Kozarac in March 1991, did you see Dule Tadic or Mira Tadic again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mira I did; Dule I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where was it that you saw Mira?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not catch the beginning of the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where did you see Mira?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Munich.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did she contact you about coming to Munich?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Why did she do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She did that because she intended to leave Dule, as she told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did she tell you why?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was it she said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She said that she caught Dule with a lover and that she had enough and that she wanted to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did she want you to sponsor her in Munich?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did that involve?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That involved a letter of guarantee so that she could come to Germany and where I would vouch that I would cover all her expenses that she might incur if she came to Germany.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did she come to Munich?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was in August of '93.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How long did she stay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Fourteen days.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At some point during her stay with you, did she indicate to you that she intended to have Dule Tadic join her?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After you learned that, did you ask her to leave and go to Mladen's?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you later learn that Dule Tadic had arrived in Munich?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That is all I have, your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Cross-examination, Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You have told the Court about your visits to Kozarac from Munich, presumably you enjoyed visiting Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Presumably, you enjoyed staying in the house of the Tadic family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You found when you stayed in their family home that the way of life in Kozarac was very different from that in Munich?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The pace of life and the people were entirely different?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Their lives were not dictated by the clock? There was less stress?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You enjoyed living that way with the Tadic family in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: A powerful influence within the family was the father of the brothers, Ostoja Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Who was a man known as a patriot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: A firm believer in the Yugoslav way of life?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: With a great commitment to the Socialist Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in communism.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: His influence on his four sons was considerable?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: He was a strong personality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, you could say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When he died it was a great sadness for the family and in the town of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Whether there was great sadness, that I do not know, but a lot of people, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you attend the funeral?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Many people in the village also attended that funeral?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Emir Karabasic was someone who carried the coffin of Ostoja Tadic along with the other brothers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Emir Karabasic did that because he was a close friend of Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Many Muslim people attended that funeral?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You agree that the vast majority of people living in the centre of Kozarac were of Muslim background?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You could not live in Kozarac without having relationships and friendships if you were a Serb with people who were Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One could.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But Muslim people used to come to Dusko Tadic's cafe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: He used to go to the cafe that was owned by another Muslim who lived nearby?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: His time was spent mixing and talking with these people daily?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you recollect when the second child of Mira and Dusko Tadic was born, what year that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: '89, '90, somewhere around there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You told us that your last visit was in March 1991, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When had you previously visited before that visit in March 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that was New Year's '90 to '91.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: For how long did you stay on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think we were always there between Christmas and New Year or maybe just for New Year. I do not recall exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Sometime perhaps amounting to about a week?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sometimes, yes, sometimes even longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In fact, did your visits to Kozarac become less frequent from 1988/1989 to what they had been in the past in the early days of your marriage with Mladen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: They were not as frequent as they had been originally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We went as often as we could.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did Mladen go without you on occasions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: He certainly went as often as he could, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He went more frequently because at that time he was not working, so he had no obligations. It was not, he was not on vacation time, so he was determining his own time for travel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In 1991 when you had that visit in the March, for how long did you stay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was for Easter and I think it was about a week.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We have heard the suggestion that you used to spend two months of the year in Kozarac. It seems certainly ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- 1991 from the New Year to the March that you had only spent two weeks for that part of the year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That year, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The previous year you did not spend as long as two months in Kozarac, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It may be. I really do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, your visits at that time, 1990, were not for as long as two months, were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Altogether throughout the whole year probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When the second child was born to Mira and Dusko Tadic, you said there was discussion of calling him Slobodan after the President Milosevic. Is there a female name for version of the name Slobodan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Slobodanka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did they call their second child Slobodanka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What is the name of President Milosevic's wife?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know Mira.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did they call the second child Mira?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What did they call the second child?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Alexandra.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Have you given television interviews concerning your connection with the Tadic family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How many?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Television interviews?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Once.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And when was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This year.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you paid for that? Were you paid money?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How many newspaper interviews have you given?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For newspapers, none.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Radio interviews?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It just seemed to me when I mentioned television interviews that you just said, "television interviews?", perhaps implying there may have been other interviews that you may have given to the media, no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No, just that one single interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You are aware of allegations against Dusko Tadic concerning violence, are you not, what has been alleged against him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You are aware that he has been alleged to have caused the genitals of a man to be castrated? You are aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You are aware of an allegation concerning an attempt to set fire to the church in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, and that is why you have told us about these incidents, that did not happen, concerning the grabbing of a man's genitals and attempting to set fire to a building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw it with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The Serbian Orthodox church in Kozarac, is that the only church in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Kozarac, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How many mosques were in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really did not count them. I do not know, many in any event.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There is no particular problem, is there, with any families seeking to go to church to have their children baptised? You do not find anything wrong with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. That is all I ask.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Ma'am, you mentioned in response to a question by Mr. Kay in connection with the funeral of Ostoja Tadic that Emir Karabasic was a close friend of Dule Tadic. You had said earlier in your testimony that they did not seem to have a close relationship. Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to my personal experience and according to what I saw there, is that Emir thought that Dule was his friend, but from Dule's side I could not see any kind of feelings or what one could see in a friendship when you feel that it works both ways.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Nothing arises, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Two questions. I hope the first one will not cause you any difficulty, but can you tell me what this expression "balija" in fact means?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is an expression, an offensive expression used for Muslims, an offensive description of a people.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: It does not have any other meaning? It is not used in any other context except as an epithet which is sometimes applied to Muslims, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: The other thing I wanted to ask you was about this house, I think prefabricated you said, in Munich where you described Tadic sprinkling petrol. Whose house was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was a house that belonged to that man Dusan Gavric. For him Dule used to work at the time.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: I see, Dule was living in that house with this man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Madam, you mentioned that you were born in Osijek in Croatia. May I know what your nationality is, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am a Croat.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Nothing, your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to this witness being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mrs. Tadic, you are permanently excused. That means you are free to leave. Thank you for coming.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you. (The witness withdrew).

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann, you have two additional witnesses and you have listed them for an hour. Tell me where we are, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: We do not think either of them will take an hour having regard to the cross-examination so far. One of them, your Honour, the witness Huebel, is still on his way from Germany. I understand that also ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: When did he start! I hope some time ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: We have had him coming for sometime, your Honour. We understand there is a problem with the translation anyway. We have to have special German translators and they will not be available until lunch time, as far as we understand, but there is one witness Reid who is ready to give evidence now.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We shall stand in recess for 15 minutes and then we will return. 11.50 a.m.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. Thank you. The next witness is Mr. Robert Reid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: I wonder if, while we are waiting, you can remind me of when it was that Mr. Tadic's father died, what month or what year?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Actually, if I remember the evidence correctly, I believe there were a couple of references to 1989. I believe there was also one reference to 1990 by one witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: It may be that I am going to get the answer from the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I believe it is 1989.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It might be 21st April 1989.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. ROBERT REID, recalled.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Reid, you may be seated. You have testified previously and I think when I had released you I did not release you permanently.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So you are still under oath. You understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. Thank you. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, you may begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Reid, as the Court correctly noted, you have testified previously and on those occasions indicated your role as the chief investigator into the investigations concerning opstina Prijedor and adjacent areas?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I would like to begin by asking you some questions about the photo book which was shown to witnesses in this case. First of all, can you tell us how many photographs are contained in the photo book?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There are 13 photographs in all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How many photographs in a photo book of that type are customary in various jurisdictions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It depends on the jurisdiction, but normally between six to eight photographs. The jurisdiction I come from, we always use eight.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Why were 13 used in this case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Through an abundance of caution.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were the persons whose pictures appeared as the other 12 photographs from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nine of the other photographs, the persons were from or born in the former Yugoslavia, one was from Rumania, one was from Morocco and the twelfth photograph we are unable to determine as the file on that person had been destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How were those photographs obtained?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Through the Dutch police.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I would like to ask you some questions about the procedure used when the photo book was shown to identification witnesses in this case, that is, witnesses who had not previously known the accused before the war. Can you tell us, first, what the procedure was when the photo book was shown to the four identification witnesses in this case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Two persons showed the book to the four witnesses. One investigator showed it to three of the witnesses and another person showed it on behalf of the ICTY. In relation to the investigator from the ICTY who showed three of the witnesses, he went to the witness and, during the course of a conversation, he said to the witness that he would like to show them a book of photographs containing photographs of 13 persons. He wanted them to look carefully at each of the photographs and if they were able to identify anybody, could they please indicate that. He further said to the witness, "Could you look through the entire book before you make a selection?"

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: With respect to the other identification witness, what procedure was employed in that case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was a procedure that I put in place and sent the photo book to the person who carried it out on behalf of the ICTY. He attended the ----

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were there any ICTY investigators in the area where the witness lived at the time the photo display was sought?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there were not. The person concerned met the witness at his place of employment. They went to a private room where the person said to the witness that he had a book of photographs that he would like to show the witness. Then he asked the witness to look through that book of photographs and if he could identify any person, could he please indicate it to him. At that particular time, it appeared to the person who was conducting the identification that the witness knew that there was a trial being carried out in The Hague, and he told the witness that that person may not be in the photo book and in any case the person carrying out the photo identification did not know if the person on trial was, in fact, in that book. He then handed the book to the witness who looked through the book -- I am sorry, prior to giving it to him, he asked him to look through the entire book first before he made any identification if he could, in fact, make that identification. It was then handed to the witness who looked through the book and when he came to the photograph -- came to a particular photograph, he said words to the effect, "That's him, that is the man that beat me and stabbed me". The person conducting the identification asked was the witness certain, and he said, yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was the person conducting the photo display himself a law enforcement official?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After the witness had an opportunity to review the photographs, as you describe, and made a selection, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The witness was then asked to sign and date the back of the photograph that he had identified. The book was then handed back to the law enforcement official. That also occurred with the other three witnesses that the ICTY investigator carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you determine whether or not upon completion of the photo display process and the selection, the identification witnesses in this case had expressed certainty or uncertainty about the selection of the photo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you determine whether or not the selection of the photo was made immediately or after a long period of deliberation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was made immediately. There was no deliberation at all from what I have been informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did the identification witnesses in this case select any other photographs in the book and advise that those were other people they recognised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In relation to the witness that the law enforcement officer carried out, he said that two of the people were familiar, but there was no recognition of those persons. In relation to the three that the investigator carried out, there were no other persons selected.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were the witnesses, the identification witnesses in this case, asked whether they knew the accused from before the war or had seen his photograph or televised image afterward?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were. They stated that they did not know him prior to the war, and that they had not seen any images within the media.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were any of the identification witnesses in this case subjected to or did they participate in repeated testing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were the identification witnesses in this case shown the photo book together with other identification witnesses or other witnesses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they were alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were the identification witnesses from the same countries or different countries?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, each of the identification witnesses is from a different country.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were any of them from [redacted]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One of them is from [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you determine whether or not the photo of the accused was displayed for a longer period of time by the investigator than any other photos in the photo array to the identification witnesses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The investigator from the ICTY and the law enforcement officer did not have control of the book. The witness had control of the book while he was looking through the book, through the photo book.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you determine whether or not the person showing the photo book indicated anything to the identification witnesses as they were looking at any of the photographs and particularly when they were looking at the photograph of the accused?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there was no indication in relation to any of the photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were any of the witnesses ever told to look at one photograph more carefully than others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you determine whether any of the identification witnesses were given positive feedback after selecting the photo of the accused?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was established and there was no feedback given to any of the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did the order of the accused's photograph in the photo lineup stay the same or did it change?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it changed. The accused's photograph was moved throughout the book for each of the witnesses and there was a separate book used for each witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were any of the identification witnesses shown a lineup of two people, a photograph or a photograph with just two people in it, for investigative purposes or for identification purposes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Are you aware that Dr. Wagenaar referred to a photograph of two persons in his report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that, and I believe that the photograph that he is referring to there is a colour photograph, a single photograph, depicting the accused with a beard with a person known as Emir Karabasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That was a photograph shown to people in Court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you determine whether or not the identification witnesses were asked if they had discussed their individual case with other witnesses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was established that they had not discussed this particular case with any other witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Other than the four identification witnesses discussed in Dr. Wagenaar's report, which was the subject of earlier testimony, was the photo book shown to any other identification witnesses ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: --- potential identification witnesses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: To how many?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could I refer to some notes that I have made in relation to this, please?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, you may.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were five other identification witnesses that it was shown to.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were recognition or identifications, rather, made in any of those cases?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, four out of the five.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Of the fifth person, was that someone who was unable to recognise anyone in the photo book?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, he could not identify anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If I may ask you one quick question about a witness named Draguna Jaskic? She was a witness who knew Mr. Tadic before the war, and was shown a photo book to which, as described in Court, she had a physical reaction and then at the end of reviewing the photo book advised that she did not recognise anyone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was she ever shown any other photo book?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, she was only ever shown one photo book and only on one occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Reid, I would like to ask you some questions about the interviews you conducted with Mr. Tadic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was Mr. Tadic advised of his rights by you at the beginning of the interviews?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were two separate interviews. There was the first interview on 9th and 10th May 1995 and a second interview on 21st and 22nd December 1995, and he was advised of his rights on both of those occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did he have counsel present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was he permitted to take breaks to consult with his attorney or for any other purpose he desired?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was it made clear that if he was not feeling well for any reason that the interviews did not have to take place or could be continued?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in fact, one interview was cancelled in October, I think it was, of 1995 as Mr. Tadic was not feeling well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was he permitted to use any notes or other material which he might wish to during the course of interviews?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I told him, I think it was in the first interview, in the very beginning, that he could use any notes to refresh his memory or anything that he wished. In the December interview, it was clear that he was using notes to refresh his memory as to times and dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may the witness be shown Exhibit 361A through C? (Handed)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you recognise those documents, Mr. Reid?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. A and C, I believe, are the documents that he was referring to. I did not actually read them, but it is consistent with the type of answers that he was giving. 361B, I am just not sure. I do not know if he had that document or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: During the course of the interview, was Mr. Tadic pressured by you into providing particular pieces of information or particular kinds of information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In particular, was he pressured into providing dates?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, the first interview was a very general interview where I wanted to, as best that we could, chronologically go through what occurred in opstina Prijedor in both the lead up to the conflict, during the conflict and after. The second interview in December of 1995 was very specific. I went immediately to the allegations that were outlined in the amended indictment, and I supplied him with dates and read to him individual allegations that were being made against him and supplied him with dates and then asked him for a response in relation to those allegations. I think the general question that I would ask at the end of an allegation, "Is there anything you wish to say in relation to that allegation?" and then Mr. Tadic would answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In the course of explaining his whereabouts on particular dates, did Mr. Tadic refer to the documents you just referenced?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the May interview, I do not believe that he had those documents. In the December interview, and particularly on 22nd December, yes, he referred to those documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Are there reflections of that in the record of interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there are.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did those indicate that Mr. Tadic in any part of the record of interview he has indicated that on a particular date he was not sure of his whereabouts, and then after reference to the document thereafter indicated a specific time and place with respect to his whereabouts at the checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. He was reminded of the document and, as a result of that reminder, he was able to go to the document and give specifics in relation to that particular allegation on a particular day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was he reminded of the document by you or by his counsel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, by his counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Tadic appear to feel hurried or rushed to provide answers to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not during the interview. He was very deliberate in his answers. If he did not understand something, he would ask for clarification. On some occasions he suggested another question. But, no, he was very deliberate throughout the interview -- through both the interviews.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we had previously indicated that we would be tendering the record of interview and I imagine this would be an appropriate time. That would be Exhibit 366.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Then 366 will be admitted. Mr. Tieger, that is the record of interview. I guess the date is indicated -- is it both interviews?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It is. Miss Sutherland is now suggesting to me, I think quite prudently, because it appears as two separate bundles, one for May and one for December, that we might want to have it marked as Exhibit 366A and B, A for the May interview and B for December.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 366 then is admitted; A will be the May and B will be the December interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am going to mark these next documents for identification only. It is more difficult to explain why at the moment, but I think we may want to change the number when these documents are admitted. So if I may have these two documents marked as 367A and B for identification only? Mr. Reid, do you recognise these documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, these are two decisions, No. 16 and No. 17, which appeared in the Banja Luka Gazette. They are decisions No. 16 of 22nd May 1992 and it relates to apartments and tenancies within opstina Prijedor. The second document, article No. 17, is dated 26th May 1992 and it is a conclusion of the regional Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region Krajina. It outlines a number of things in relation to the recommendation of judges and prosecutors for the basic courts. It then outlines that leading posts in the social and public organisations can be occupied only by the most professional cadre that is absolutely loyal to the Serb people in the Serb Republic Bosnia and Herzegovina. It then outlines about management boards in stock companies, the control of people in the communes, a committee to be formed for negotiations with members of other nationalities, an agency that would work on the problem of population immigration and a paragraph in relation to sales tax -- two paragraphs actually in relation to sales tax.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Reid, what is the Banja Luka Gazette?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Banja Luka Gazette is the official organ, if I can put it that way, of the Autonomous Region Krajina and it is usually for decisions, conclusions, all the official communications of the regional Crisis -- among other bodies, the regional Crisis Staff for the Autonomous Region of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wish to tender these documents, but I should indicate (and that is why I made the point about identification) that these are English translations of portions of Exhibit 145. I did not know if the Court wanted to have them marked accordingly as a portion of 145 or just proceed chronologically. I am not sure there is a perfect solution, but I wanted to leave that to the Court.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I do not know. I do not have a preference. 145, we do not have it as an A or B. It is just 145. Do you know, Mr. Bos?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, it is just one -- it is a bundle of papers marked as one exhibit and not ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: This would be then the English translation of portions of decisions in there?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes. If I remember correctly, there are English translations which comprise part of Exhibit 145 already.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I do not know. Why do we not leave it as it is? This way we will know that they are English translations of the decisions 16 and 17. I gather 16 and 17, the Serbo-Croat, are in 145?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Cyrillic.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Cyrillic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, yes. It is in Cyrillic. The entire Gazette that we have is in Cyrillic. There are a number of individual English translations of those decisions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Let us leave it the way it is then. It will be 367A and B and we understand what it is, only because we do not have 145 before us and we will have to look at that and see how it might relate. Just leave it this way. Is there any objection to 367A and B?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: They will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Reid, are you familiar with two witnesses who testified in this case, Hakija Elezovic and Samir Hodzic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not they lived in the same country at the time they gave their initial statements?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they did not. They lived on separate continents.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did they continue to live on separate continents thereafter as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know the distance from Sisak to Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: I am sorry. I do not know if I followed that last answer. They no longer live in separate continents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They live in the same area currently, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You mean the same area as they previously did?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, one -- they live together now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the distance from Sisak to Kozarac is approximately 70 kilometres as the crow flies. It would probably be at the very, very most an hour and a half, two hour, drive between the two locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to examine the unredacted traffic police rosters which were obtained during the course of the video link testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I have not examined the entire roster, but I have examined a couple of pages of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In examining portions of that roster of traffic policemen, did you find the names of any persons who were reported to have been involved in the round-up or selection of Muslims to go to camps or any other aspect of the ethnic cleansing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Can I refer to the document that I have?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The document that I was given, on the very first page, 16th June 1992, there are two names there, at No. 706 the Kozarac checkpoint, Zeljko Maric. Statements have been taken from at least three witnesses that implicate that person in the roundup of people fleeing from Kozarac. The other person that is on this roster is marked No. 3 under the heading "slobodni" which, I believe, means "day off" or "rest day". It is No. 3, Bosko Grabez. We have a number of statements from witnesses who were taken from the Omarska camp to Manjaca camp on 6th August 1992 where that person travelled on one of the buses as a guard on the bus. There are further statements from witnesses that say that that person was involved in the murder of a person at the front of Manjaca camp on the night of 6th August/morning of 7th August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Which Exhibit is that? Do you have an Exhibit number on that roster?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: 66C, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I missed it, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: D66C, I should add.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: I am afraid I missed the second name, Grabez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Grabez, your Honour, yes, spelt G-R-A-B-E-Z.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I think there is an error on the transcript which had it down as Bosko Dragicevic who is someone else entirely.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me have a moment, your Honour. I apologise, your Honour, I am sorry. Your Honour, may I have these marked as 368A through D? Mr. Reid, are these articles from Kosarksi Vjesnik in which there are photographs depicting persons in various uniforms at various times?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am going to tender those Exhibits. They really speak for themselves and also I will be submitting some colour photographs of uniforms as well in response to the Court's request.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 368A and B will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Those will be A through D, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 368A through D then are admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think this can be submitted as simply Exhibit 369. The Defence may want to take a look at that. They are just photographs of various uniforms. Mr. Reid, in 369 do you see any photographs showing an SMB uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the first five photographs they are SMB uniforms and the one on top is the winter uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can we have one of those placed on the overhead projector, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the winter uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It looks like it is not going to happen, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: However you want to handle it; if you wish, you can just hand them up to the Bench and we will take a look at them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Reid, does 369 show the SMB uniform and various camouflage uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the last two photographs in the pile are the camouflage uniforms of the former JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The previous Exhibit, did the photographs in those Exhibits or that Exhibit also depict soldiers in both SMB and camouflage uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. There is one there that I noticed where there is a unit being inspected and there were soldiers within that unit wearing civilian clothes as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I imagine the Court will have time to review that at its leisure.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It is working, if you want to show us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the winter uniform of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Does "SMB" refer to the particular style of uniform or to the colour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I think it is the colour. It is the particular colour that they refer to. They never say an olive green or a green or a black or a grey. It is always an SMB uniform and it always refers to the JNA uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I understand there are also a couple of photographs showing one or another type of camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: The witness mentioned that one photograph was the winter uniform. This is the first I have heard of a winter uniform. Is that a winter SMB or just ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I believe, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As distinct from a summer SMB?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. The summer is, I believe, something like this photograph here and, additionally, this photograph here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: That is a different colour. How do you differentiate this uniform from the previous ones?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry, your Honour?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How do you differentiate this uniform from the previous one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the previous uniform of the JNA. This is -- I believe that this would be like equivalent to a dress uniform or a full uniform, if you like. This -- I believe this type of uniform is the battle uniform or one that would be used out in the field or around the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The colours are different?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, but they are still described by witnesses as "SMB".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The camouflage uniforms, and the .....

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was that tendered, your Honour?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It has not been admitted, I do not think, 369. Is there any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Reid, did you review information or have access to information which would indicate whether or not any prisoners who were held in the large hangar building of the Omarska camp were held in portions of the ground floor located to the left of the entrance as one would enter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do not believe that there were prisoners held in those rooms. The statements that I have looked at, which is every statement that has been taken, no witness has actually said they have been held in that -- in any of those rooms. On the inspection that we did of the large hangar in February and March of this year, it appeared as though a lot of those rooms were where they stored tools, machinery and things like that and they were still basically intact from when it was no longer used as a mine but as a camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did the information indicate whether or not any prisoners were held between the area of the entrance and the stairway room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again, there is a large room that has -- there was -- when you go into that room which is pretty much in the middle of that area you are describing, there was a large board with all the names of the workers that either worked in the hangar or the entire mine, I am not sure. That was also an area that housed all the tools and different machines, lathes and things like that, and it appeared as though it had not been used as a room when Omarska was a camp. There were, in fact, people working in that when we were doing our inspection.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That is all I have, your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Cross-examination, Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just a few questions on the last matters you raised, Mr. Reid. You are referring, presumably, to your observations during your visit of February 1996 ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- which was obviously some considerable period of time since the closure of Omarska as a detention camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was closed somewhere around 21st/22nd August 1992. There are a lot of things there though that appeared to be that people had just up and left. There is an area upstairs, the internal stairway, the offices above in that area, there were still desk calendars within the last week of May 1992. There were documents just spread out over desks and it appeared as though that area had not been used either. So it was consistent that there had not really been anybody up in that area as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps people may not have been held in those rooms for any significant period, but that is not to say that for periods of time people may have been put in those rooms, perhaps not as permanent places of detention, but they may have been put in there for whatever reason?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The same goes for the ground floor as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It does seem that on occasions the hangar building has been used by various organisations or people since that period of August 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct. When I was there in February/March, there was a clear line of demarkation, if you like. The bottom level and the internal stairway and the rooms above the internal stairway were being used by the Omarska mine ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: --- and the area from the external stairway that led up to the first floor was being used by the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: They, in fact, were using the hangar building, as we are familiar with it in this courtroom, as an ammunition store?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that is what it may be now. There was ammunition there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But the ammunition store, no, was in the administration building, in the room that has become known as "Mujo's room". That was where the ammunition store was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you went there in February, were there vast boxes full of weapons or ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Mujo's room there was, yes, which is in the administration building or the restaurant building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So it seems that there has been certainly people entering this particular camp and using it for other purposes since the days of August 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now a couple of other questions about other matters. I think I will start with the photo procedures. You have referred to an investigator, presumably, from the Prosecution team and a separate investigator, as a law enforcement officer, who undertook the identification procedures in relation to the four witnesses who claimed not to have known Dusko Tadic before the conflict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: First of all, the name of the person from the Office of the Prosecutor or the Prosecution team, who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is Mr. Thomas Ackheim.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The name of the other person who was a law enforcement officer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Is Mr. Ron Safer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Spelt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: S-A-F-E-R.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were there other law enforcement officers or investigators from the Prosecution used in relation to these procedures?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only from the Office of the Prosecutor. There was no other outside law enforcement body used to show the photo spreads. That was the only photospread.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We heard evidence from a man called Jos Paepen ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- who was involved in one identification process. It seemed to have been his only contact with this particular area. Was he an outside law enforcement officer or did he work for the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he worked for the Office of the Prosecutor. He was an investigator or was at that time an investigator with the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How many such officers are we concerned with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The other officer that showed photospreads was Mr. Grant McIntosh who is the other investigator on the team.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When these identification procedures were carried out -- we are essentially considering the four that you have given evidence about ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- were notes taken at the time of the procedures that were followed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that Mr. Safer made notes and Mr. Ackheim, no, he did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When the identification procedures were carried out, was there any filming of how they were gone about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was there any recording of the length of time for which the witness was considering the pages of the photospread?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At what stage during the contact with the witness was the identification book used to enable the procedure to take place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can I refer to my notes?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
