utterances.text: Thank you. In relation to three of the witnesses, a statement was obtained and then the photo book was shown to them sometime after. In relation to the fourth witness, the photo book was shown during the interview of that witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you able to help us with the stage of the interview at which the book was shown?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot say positively, but I believe that in relation to the witness that was shown the photo book during the interview it was at the end of the interview, the conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The names of the four witnesses we are concerned with here, if you can perhaps give them to us now so that we have them in our minds?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sure. The first witness that I speak of is Kasim Mesic, the second one is Sejad Halvadzic, the third one is Senad Muslimovic and the fourth one is Zemka Sahbaz.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Of those the one handled by the independent law enforcement officer was which?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Muslimovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did the officers of the investigation section of the Prosecution team have any pre-written form of words that they had to use in relation to these procedures? Is there a document that set out the precise wording for them to use and the procedures to be followed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there is not. It is an experience thing. For instance, if I was to show a photo book I really would not need anything written down. It is the same as a record of interview, a handwritten statement, anything like that. I have done it so often. It is an experience thing that you can just go through it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You are familiar, it seems, with procedures that are used in different parts of the world. You told us about the six to eight photographs that may be used by many different jurisdictions as generally the normal spread?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Other jurisdictions have procedures that are set out, pro forma documents, that investigating officers use and follow down the page each instruction which is signed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Each individual police force (and the police force I come from) has a set of guidelines, and they are guidelines. You are taught them from the day you join the police until the day you retire, but on occasions the guidelines do vary depending on the witness. For instance, the guidelines for a lineup, they say that the witness should go across, in a physical lineup, a live lineup, the witness should go across to the accused person and touch that person on the shoulder. Some witnesses, particularly sexual assault victims, cannot do that, so they -- so you have to vary the guidelines. It just -- it depends on each individual witness how you do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So in relation to the procedures we are concerned with for these four witnesses, there was no protocol that was written out that established the guidelines to be used by those two officers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. With Mr. Safer, I am sorry, there were, there were written guidelines for him to follow, and they were sent to him with the photo book as to how to run through it, and that was the sole purpose of Mr. Safer seeing Mr. Muslimovic, was to show him the photo book.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What did the guides lines say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Basically what I have outlined. If I could refer to another document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Is this a letter to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, it is not a letter. It is a conversation that I had with him, but he followed it basically to the letter of the law. It is basically what I have outlined in my evidence earlier, that he asked him to look through the book to see if he recognised anyone. I also asked him that if he did recognise anybody, to indicate how he knew that person. Mr. Safer said that, and this is where it varies, the guidelines vary, it appeared quite openly to Mr. Safer that Mr. Muslimovic knew there was a trial going on, so he varied the guidelines that we had given him in that case. He also told him, and we did not tell Mr. Safer whether Mr. Tadic was in the book at all, and then how to go through, handing the book, let him go through it and not to let him spend a lot of time looking at it, and I mean a lot of time to me is to a witness who is perhaps an eyewitness 10 minutes is a long time, from experience. Normally, a person can identify a person fairly quickly, from experience, and that was what -- the guidelines that we set for him. I asked him to have him sign and date any photograph that he identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So the period of time that seems to have been applied by your investigation team is about 10 minutes for the photo book, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, that is my own guideline. I would never or very, very rarely let a witness go even that long looking at a photo book. I think, having spoken to Mr. Ackheim, the entire procedure with the three witnesses that he showed from the time that he handed the witness the book to when they flick through it, looked at each of the photographs, identified the photograph, signed and dated it was somewhere in the vicinity of three minutes. That was an average.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The witness Muslimovic who was aware of the trial that was going on, he was obviously aware that it was the trial of Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At what stage then was he put through this procedure?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: His photo board was on 9th May, yes, 9th May, 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So after the opening of the case, the trial starting on 7th May?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He was interviewed in March, I think, of 1996 -- yes, March 1996 he was interviewed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The country that he was living in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He is still living there, so I prefer not to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Which one is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The other three witnesses that were dealt with by the investigator, were they shown the photo book before the trial had started or after the trial had started? Perhaps you can give us the dates for each of those witnesses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mesic was shown the photo book on 12th June 1996, Mr. Halvadzic was shown the photo book on 14th June 1996, and Mrs. Sahbaz was shown the book on 31st May 1996. In relation to Mr. Mesic and Mr. Halvadzic, they were shown the book when they were actually here in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Presumably, when they were shown the book in The Hague, they knew why they had come to The Hague, whose trial it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It was not a secret?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No. Mr. Sahbaz?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mrs. Sahbaz.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mrs. Sahbaz, sorry. She was shown the photo book on 31st May 1996?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When had she given her statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She gave her statement on 31st May 1996 as well. We had only just found her at that particular time and she was interviewed immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So that was all done at the same time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Draguna Jaskic, is there any indication that she has a connection or association with any of the other witnesses in the case of Mr. Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She is the sister -- in relation to these identification witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She lived in the same village, I believe, or in the close proximity to Mrs. Sahbaz, but with the other witnesses, no, I do not believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is Mrs. Sahbaz who did the identification on 31st May ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I thought you were talking about the four identification witnesses. Mrs. Sahbaz would be the only one that she would have any knowledge of, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: She may have connections with other witnesses, but of this group of four ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- it is the case that it is Mrs. Sahbaz with whom she also has a connection?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and I do not know what the connection is today. I know that they lived in the same village or they lived in either Sivci or Jaskici which are in close proximity to each other, but that is basically it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Could one be the sister of the other or sister-in-law?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not believe she is the sister-in-law. The sister of Draguna Jaskic is Subha Mujic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, there is one other matter. We have produced the interviews of Mr. Tadic for May and December ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- of last year. I am just checking really that they are a complete set because there was a defect in the camera?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on the first interview in May the main camera malfunctioned but we had a backup camera, and I think you will find that as tape 5A, I believe. That is complete -- I have checked -- and the interview is complete.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The copies their Lordships have been given is a complete transcript?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of the entire ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Without missing pages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just one other matter as it occurs to me: Witness L, was he taken out to Trnopolje to identify places or sites?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Who took him out to the opstina Prijedor region?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did, among other people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was that part of a Prosecution visit to the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I took him out. It was arranged specifically to take him to the area and I did that, I believe, on 2nd October of this year.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Of this year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am actually thinking of slightly before the time that we have had the revelation of the issues.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was he taken out before the trial started or before he gave evidence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You have been aware of his movements, have you, since he was given to you by the Bosnian police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. That satisfies me. There has been discussion, as you are aware, between the Defence on the number of witnesses in particular countries and I believe you have talked to Mr. Wladimiroff about this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am wondering whether the list has been prepared to advise us of the geographic distribution in relation to witnesses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can tell you the number of witnesses from each of the countries.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If that is what you are looking for. I can tell you a breakdown of those witnesses and I have only included fact witnesses, not policy or expert witnesses. [redacted]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [redacted]. I might add that they are the countries where the people were interviewed and statements were taken from them. They do not necessarily live in those countries now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At this particular time would they have been interviewed in the countries in which they were living at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That is the breakdown I have just given you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. That is all I ask.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: First, your Honour, before I begin can I ask for a redaction at 15.05.26. Mr. Reid, just one matter. You were asked about Draguna Jaskic and Mrs. Sahbaz?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You indicated you thought they were from the same place, that is Jaskici or Sivci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes. Do you know whether or not they were living in the same country thereafter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they do not live in the same country now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you. That is all.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do you have any objection to that redaction?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That will be granted. Do you have additional questions, Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: A couple of questions, Mr. Reid. The first one was looking across the Court at the model of Omarska there, the large apparently two-storey building at the far end of the hangar we seem to have heard nothing at all about in evidence. Was it entirely separate from the longitudinal part of the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is one door that connects the two buildings and there is no information from any witness that I have seen that that was ever used.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you. The other thing I wanted to ask was what you have told us about the procedure with the photospread is entirely what you have been informed by the two different officers who conducted it? You were not present at any of these photospread examinations, were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: How many different officers conducted it? One who was an independent law enforcement officer and then who else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With the four identification witnesses there were only two people involved. One is Mr. Ackheim who showed three witnesses and the other is Mr. Safer who showed Mr. Muslimovic.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, do you have additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: One moment, your Honour. No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger did you have additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Reid is permanently excused, I presume?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you for coming. You are excused from coming.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. (The witness withdrew).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, you have been good enough to give us Exhibit 366A and B each of which is very lengthy. This is really to help in view of the 6,000 plus pages of transcript that we already have. Will you be drawing our attention to particular passages in the final address of these or are we expected to examine them and compare them with the evidence? What is your intention in giving them to us now?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, you may be sure that we will be drawing the Court's attention to particular portions of that document. You may recall that that was done during cross-examination as well, and we will give the Court as much guidance as possible in utilizing the evidence which has been presented in a most efficient form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: We will look forward to that with interest. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, would you call your next witness or Mr. Keegan?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: I apologise for this late notice to the Court and also to the Defence. Your Honour, I was literally just informed by the witness who is a German police officer that he requests facial distortion during his testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We, you need to talk with opposing counsel about that and we will stand in recess for five minutes and see if it can be agreed upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. 3.15 p.m. (The Court adjourned for a short time). 3.20 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the record I should indicate that during the recess we requested and were granted without objection a redaction from 15.11.48 to 15.12.46.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That has been granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Keegan, would you call the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. I call Officer Huebel to the stand, please.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: There is no objection to facial distortion?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour. ALFRED HUEBEL, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sir, would you please take the oath that is being handed to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I shall tell the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Sir, would you please state your full name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Alfred Huebel is my name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What position do you currently hold, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am Chief Investigator in Mecklenheim.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: How long have you held that position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have been with the federal investigation there since 1980.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Sir, on 11 and 12 October of 1994 did you conduct an interview of Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With my colleague Officer Balante and myself on that date, we did question Mr. Tadic in Munich in the Stadelheim facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Do you see the man that you interviewed on that day here in this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I see Mr. Tadic on my left, here in the middle between the other two gentlemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: OK. I need you, if you would please, to point at him and if you could just describe what he is wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tadic is wearing a grey suit. He is wearing a blue shirt and a dark tie.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if the record could reflect that the witness identified the accused?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, the record will so reflect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Could Prosecution Exhibit 321A be given to the witness, please? (Handed). Sir, if you could look at the document that has been handed to you and tell me if you recognise it, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document here before me is the record of the interview that was carried out by myself and by my colleague in the prison facility in Munich at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Sir, if I could ask you to turn to page 18 of that document, it is marked "18" in the bottom right-hand corner of your document. If page 11 could be placed on the Elmo, please, of the English version. Thank you. Sir, if you look at that page 18 in that record of interview. You asked the accused about a document identified as Exhibit 1.12.87 which had been seized from the apartment in Munich where the accused was staying. That document refers to the issuance of an automatic weapon and 300 rounds of ammunition to the accused. When you were referring to that document and your questions to the accused, did you show that document to the accused?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We did show that document to Mr. Tadic. He did have an opportunity to see it and become acquainted with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you follow that practice for each of the documents which are referred to in the questions in this record of interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now the Exhibits which are referred to in this document were all produced to Mr. Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Is that a requirement of the operating procedures for the German police authorities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is a procedure that is followed by the German police in such cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: If Exhibit 148 could be shown to the witness, please, Prosecution Exhibit 148. The plastic sleeve must also be shown to the witness. Sir, do you recognise that Exhibit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now on the plastic cover there is a sticker that we put on exhibits. It is my colleague that signed it here. The Exhibit I have here was produced to Mr. Tadic at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Nothing further, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you would like to look at the first page of the questioning of the accused, which is page 3 in the bottom right-hand corner ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: This is 321A, is it or 321 I guess?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: In his language. OK, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It is headed about "About the Individual". I think it is page 2 of the German document. Can you see that, Officer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have page 2 open here, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It states as a comment there that Mr. Tadic was given an opportunity to acquaint himself with the second letter he sent from prison dated 6th March 1994, and agreed to those handwritten 10 pages being included as attachment one. It says that they are included as a seven-page translation by the interpreter Mr. Kertes. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That specifically refers to a document that was produced to Mr. Tadic during the interview, does it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was something that had been drafted by Mr. Tadic and that was annexed to the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But it says here he was given an opportunity to acquaint himself with the second letter. Does that not mean he was given an opportunity during the interview to look at that document and that was recorded in the interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I would point out that I am afraid I have not understood your question as put.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, what I am curious about is why you say this document was produced during the interview and it does not say that it was produced before him. On page 11 that we have been looking at where you have been asked to consider this Exhibit, it does not state that it was produced before him, does it?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I think he is still looking at page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. If you would like to look at page 17 of the German document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am looking at that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It does not say it was actually produced for him to look at, does it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can just repeat what I said earlier on, the document was produced and Mr. Tadic did have an opportunity to acquaint himself with that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How many other documents were then produced during this interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I already indicated that. All of the exhibits that have their own reference number were produced in the course of the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. That is all I ask.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Keegan?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Officer Huebel, the production of specific exhibits or documents referred to, you testified earlier is the standard procedure for German police authorities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a standard procedure in Germany when reference is made to exhibits, and when there is any need to mention exhibits those exhibits are produced to the person involved and the person involved is given a chance to look at them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: The accused had a Defence counsel present during this interview, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During the three days of interviews, from the first to the last minute the German Defence counsel of Mr. Tadic was present throughout. He could follow the proceedings and he had the opportunity to make any objections he might have cared to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: This first document which the Defence counsel asked you about which was attached as an annex, that was in fact separate, if you will, from the actual interview itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was a separate matter because in those handwritten notes Mr. Tadic had made some statements about himself and about his activities, and that is why that was referred to in the part entitled "About the Individual".

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: In the comment that follows there are additions or corrections, if you will, that the accused himself wanted to make for the record?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What was entered into further on is a fuller understanding of the elements relating to the individual Mr. Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Nothing further, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You have just told us that Mr. Tadic was interviewed over three days, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right, Mr. Tadic was questioned over a three-day period.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How many pages of interview do we have for that questioning during the period of three days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now I have here the front page 1 to 31 and that is the full record, the full transcript of the interview of Mr. Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you refer to this passage of the interview at page 11, page 17 of your document, it does not say that Mr. Tadic looked at the document, does it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can just reiterate what I have already said and repeat that Mr. Tadic did see that document. It was produced.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, there is a difference between a document being produced and a document being looked at. You understand that difference, do you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Tadic was shown this document and he had the opportunity to examine it more closely and read what it said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So when you say he had the opportunity to examine it more closely and see what it said, that does not mean that he did look at it more closely?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We gave him the opportunity to look at the document, to read it, and Mr. Tadic did see the document and Mr. Tadic could read the document. He was granted the time and the possibility to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: His reply was he knew nothing about it and he did not receive any weapons or any ammunition from the staff of the Territorial Defence, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is also what we put in the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Keegan?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: No nothing, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sir, you are permanently excused. You are free to leave, but you need to remain where you are sitting. The Judges will leave so that we can then go back into open session. So you remain where you are sitting, but you are free to go after we have left. 3.50 p.m. (The Court adjourned for a short time). 3.55 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the one thing remaining I think is that there was a piece of paper shown, two pieces of paper shown to Witness AA this morning and I tender those. Might they be given collectively the number 370? They are just two pieces of paper with names on them, your Honours. Might they be sealed?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, they will be marked as Prosecution 370 and 371 or together?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: 370A and B.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: They will be admitted and sealed.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there anything else, Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, your Honours, that concludes the evidence of the Prosecution in rebuttal.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. We will not call for evidence in rejoinder, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The Chamber wants to thank counsel, of course, for the very professional way that you presented the evidence. We have scheduled closing arguments for November 25th at 10 a.m. and have reserved two days, but we are willing to go to three days to listen to you for as long as you wish. So we encourage you to take your time and present the evidence fully. It has been a long trial with a number of Exhibits and many thousands of pages of testimony. We will adjourn then until November 25th at 10 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: (The Court adjourned for a short time)
